rubric_items.reason: CO-1..CO-7 and EP-1 are all in the diff as designed: activeOnWeekday, onDutyToday reusing slotStates/occupyingBetween, Dashboard.onDuty, shared DoctorService, web type and section.
SQL stays in the repository, rules in the service, camelCase response fields, strict types; no contact data copied, matching DSH-9.
8 files, all named by the design; the only test edit is the required onDuty field on the typed Dashboard fixture.
Empty list, Fully booked, PAST-at-now and null next slot are handled; minor edge: the dashboard and onDutyToday read the clock separately, so today can differ at midnight.
Summary and per-file Changes list match the diff file by file, including the stable-sort tie-break and the fixture edit.

findings.text: activeOnWeekday loads blocks with one availability query per doctor, so a dashboard load costs 2N extra queries; the design trade-off only accepted N occupyingBetween queries.

cites.quote: at the cost of N small queries per dashboard load

findings.suggested_fix: Load all blocks for the selected doctors in one query (doctor_id = ANY($1)) and group them, or note the extra N queries as a trade-off.

findings.text: DashboardService derives today from its own clock() call and onDutyToday calls clock() again, so a request straddling local midnight can return a today field and onDuty rows for different days.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the already-read now (or today) from DashboardService.get() into onDutyToday(now).
